question: Does WooCommerce Subscriptions Work With WooCommerce Memberships?
metaDescription: WooCommerce Memberships and Subscriptions are built by the same team to work together — linking a membership to a subscription grants access automatically.
shortAnswer: Yes — WooCommerce Memberships is specifically designed to integrate with WooCommerce Subscriptions, so a membership plan can be tied to a subscription product: purchasing the subscription grants the membership, and cancelling, pausing, or a failed renewal on the subscription updates the membership's access automatically, without custom code required for the basic case.

bodyHtml:
How It Works

When creating a membership plan, WooCommerce Memberships offers an option to grant access via purchasing a specific product — if that product is a WooCommerce Subscriptions product, the membership becomes tied to the subscription's lifecycle rather than a one-time purchase. Access starts when the subscription becomes active, and the membership plan can be configured to pause or end access automatically when the subscription is put on hold, cancelled, or expires.

What to Configure Deliberately

  • What happens to access during a failed-payment retry period. Whether membership access pauses immediately on the first failed attempt or only after retries are exhausted is a configuration choice worth making deliberately, not leaving at whatever the default happens to be.
  • Content drip schedules (if the membership plan releases content over time) interacting with a paused-then-resumed subscription — test whether a pause also pauses the drip schedule or lets it continue counting.
  • Multiple subscription tiers mapping to different membership levels, which needs each tier's product linked to the correct corresponding plan rather than assuming one setup covers every tier.
  • What happens on a plan switch (a customer upgrading or downgrading their subscription) — confirm membership access updates correctly to match the new tier, not just the old one persisting.

Setting It Up Correctly

  1. Link the membership plan to the subscription product explicitly under the plan's Access settings, rather than assuming proximity in the same store is enough.
  2. Test the full lifecycle — signup, a simulated failed payment, cancellation, and resubscription — confirming membership access follows correctly at each stage.
  3. For multiple tiers, test each one independently to confirm the right plan activates for the right subscription product.
  4. Document the access rules (what happens on hold, on cancellation, on switch) somewhere the support team can reference, since these edge cases are common sources of customer confusion otherwise.

See custom WooCommerce development for a membership-and-subscription setup with rules beyond what the standard integration configures out of the box.
